questions.stem: As per Article 151 of the Indian Constitution, the audit reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) are submitted to whom?

options.option_text: Speaker of Lok Sabha, who tables them in the Lower House
Finance Minister, for review before tabling in Parliament
President of India, who causes them to be laid before Parliament
Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee in Parliament

questions.explanation: Article 151 mandates that CAG reports relating to Union accounts be submitted to the President, who shall cause them to be laid before each House of Parliament. Option B (Finance Minister) is wrong because the CAG is constitutionally independent of the executive — the Finance Ministry has no role in the submission chain.

questions.stem: The 'India State of Forest Report (ISFR)', a biennial assessment of forest and tree cover across India, is published by which organisation?

options.option_text: Wildlife Institute of India (WII), headquartered in Dehradun
Forest Survey of India (FSI), under the Ministry of Environment
National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) under MoEFCC
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change directly

questions.explanation: ISFR is published by Forest Survey of India (FSI), a body under MoEFCC, using satellite-based assessment to map forest and tree cover biennially. Option A (WII) is a common distractor — WII conducts wildlife research and tiger/elephant censuses, not forest cover mapping; that mandate belongs exclusively to FSI.

questions.stem: The 'National Family Health Survey (NFHS)', which provides data on population, health, and nutrition indicators across Indian households, falls under which nodal Ministry?

options.option_text: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India
Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)
Ministry of Women and Child Development, North Block
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India

questions.explanation: NFHS is conducted under MoHFW with IIPS (International Institute for Population Sciences), Mumbai as the nodal implementing agency. Option B (MoSPI) is the most tempting wrong answer because MoSPI handles the NSS and most household surveys — but NFHS specifically sits under the health ministry because its primary focus is health and nutrition data.

questions.stem: The 'World Economic Outlook (WEO)', a flagship report frequently cited in India's Annual Economic Survey for global growth projections, is released by which body?

options.option_text: World Bank's Development Economics Research Group (DECRG)
International Monetary Fund (IMF), published biannually each year
World Economic Forum, Davos, released every January in Davos
United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD)

questions.explanation: WEO is an IMF flagship publication released twice a year (April and October), providing GDP forecasts and macroeconomic analysis for member countries. Option C (WEF/Davos) is a common error — WEF publishes the Global Competitiveness Report and Global Risks Report; WEO is strictly an IMF document. Option A (World Bank) publishes the World Development Report.

questions.stem: The National Statistical Office (NSO), India's apex body for official statistics, was constituted in May 2019 by merging which two premier organisations?

options.option_text: Planning Commission data wing and NITI Aayog statistics division
Central Statistics Office (CSO) and National Sample Survey Office (NSSO)
Reserve Bank of India's DBIE unit and Central Statistics Office
Registrar General of India and the Census Commissioner's offices

questions.explanation: NSO was formed by merging the CSO (which compiled national accounts, IIP, and CPI) with the NSSO (which conducted large-scale household surveys), both under MoSPI. Option D is wrong — the Registrar General of India and Census Commissioner remain a separate statutory office under the Ministry of Home Affairs and were not part of this merger.

questions.stem: Under the CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India holds office for a term of:

options.option_text: Five years or until attaining 60 years of age, whichever is earlier
Five years or until attaining 65 years of age, whichever is earlier
Six years or until attaining 65 years of age, whichever is earlier
Six years or until attaining 62 years of age, whichever is earlier

questions.explanation: Section 4 of the CAG's (DPC&S) Act, 1971 prescribes a term of 6 years OR age 65, whichever comes first. Option B (5 years/65) is the most tempting wrong answer — students confuse the 5-year term with other constitutional posts or confuse 65 with the correct age but pair it with the wrong number of years. The CAG is also constitutionally barred from holding further office under the Union or any State Government after retirement.

questions.stem: The Annual Survey of Industries (ASI), India's primary source of data on the organised manufacturing sector, covers factories registered under which sections of the Factories Act, 1948?

options.option_text: Section 85, which allows state governments to extend Act coverage
Section 7A, dealing with occupier obligations in notified industries
Sections 2m(i) and 2m(ii), defining a 'factory' under the Act
Sections 11 and 12, governing cleanliness and health in factories

questions.explanation: ASI covers factories registered under Sections 2m(i) [10 or more workers using power] and 2m(ii) [20 or more workers without power] of the Factories Act, 1948 — these two sub-sections formally define what constitutes a 'factory'. Option A (Section 85) is the most tempting distractor: Section 85 lets state governments extend the Act to smaller establishments, but these are an optional add-on coverage layer and not the primary definitional basis of ASI's survey universe.
